messages.subject: Access input$... in ui.R
parts:
Hi all,

I am just discovering Shiny and loving it. So first off, thanks very much!

Now, I have created an app which reads a file with time series for a large number of variables, offers to select a few variables through checkboxGroupInput() and plots the corresponding time series (using ggplot + facet_grid).

So my `ui.R` looks basically like:

load("mydata.Rdata")
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  sidebarPanel(
    checkboxGroupInput("vars", "Vars", names(mydata))
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("seriesPlot")
  )
))

Of course, since the height of plotOutput is fixed, the height of each series (each facet) becomes smaller when more variables are selected. I would like the height of the plot to grow with the number of variables selected. I don't need it to be very precise, so, for example, I would be very happy to have

    plotOutput("seriesPlot", height=length(input$vars) * 100)

to allocate ~100px per variable. But the `input` variable is unknown at this point.

How could I achieve this?
Thank you very much in advance!

Jean-Olivier Irisson

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Access input$... in ui.R
parts:
Hi Jean-Olivier -

It's not possible to use input$ variables directly in ui.r, since the code in ui.r simply generates an HTML page. However, you can use the approach discussed here (you've probably read this already, but just in case...):

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/4E5rJlHlnZA/discussion


To make it work, you'll need to get the latest version of Shiny from github. Good luck!

-Winston

Thanks Winston. I did not read this topic no. I was searching for a more generic answer. But it is indeed exactly what I need and it works with the latest version of shiny. So thanks a lot.

Still, the more general problem is of interest to me since, for a different application, I have this use case:

the user selects various variables in a dataset (various species) and the same analysis is run for each of these species. For each analysis/species, I want to output a summary text and a few plots. So I would want to loop over input$species and call textOutput and several plotOutput for each of them successively.

The only way that I see to achieve this currently is to prepare n (10 or so) textOutput + plotOutput calls, let the user select m species (with m <= n) and fill the first m calls with something, while leaving the rest blank. Not very elegant or scalable. What could be a better solution?

Thanks in advance!

Jean-Olivier Irisson
